nodes.name: Electrode Preparation and Cleaning
nodes.procedure: The Pt thin film working electrode was prepared by a typical two-step deposition method, involving the chemical deposition of an Au thin film on a hemispheric Si prism followed by the galvanostatic electrodeposition of a Pt thin film on the Au substrate. Before electrochemical and spectroscopic tests, the prepared Pt thin film working electrode was firstly cycled in Ar-saturated 0.1 M AMOH electrolyte between 0.02 V and 1.2 V at a scan rate of 100 mV s-1 for two cycles to get a clean surface.

nodes.name: Computational Interface Construction
nodes.procedure: To mimic the Pt/AMOHaq (AM+ = Li+, Na+, K+) interfaces, 60 water molecules were placed above a Pt(111) slab (four-layer 4x4 orthogonal, 1.10 nm^2 surface area); then, several AM+ cations were progressively inserted into the water layer at ~ 3–4 Å away from the electrode surface. For HER/HOR interfaces, hydrogen adsorbates (H_ad) with coverage of 0.63 ML and 0.25 ML were included. Electrode potential was calculated using the work function difference between the interface and SHE (4.44 V).

nodes.characterization_summary: AIMD simulations reveal cation-dependent electric double layer (EDL) structures where larger cations induce wider water gap zones (0.27 Å for Li+, 0.63 Å for Na+, and 1.03 Å for K+) and greater H-bond network discontinuity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: widths of gap zones are estimated to be 0.27 Å, 0.63 Å and 1.03 Å at Pt(111)/LiOHaq, Pt(111)/NaOHaq and Pt(111)/KOHaq interfaces, respectively, through integrating the water concentration distribution profiles.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ SEIRAS confirms that the proportion of H-bond-poor (HB-poor) interfacial water increases with alkali metal cation size (LiOH < NaOH < KOH), correlating with the width of the simulated gap zone.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ SEIRAS spectra recorded at potentials ... average proportions of HB-poor H2O obtained from electrochemical in situ spectroscopy ... exhibit a distinct linear relationship with the simulated width of the gap zone.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cyclic voltammetry shows typical polycrystalline Pt features and confirms that the HER kinetics decrease in the order LiOH > NaOH > KOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: prepared Pt thin-film working electrode can exhibit typical cyclic voltammogram features of polycrystalline Pt surfaces, and the HER rate does decrease in the order LiOH > NaOH > KOH

nodes.characterization_summary: Hydrogen binding energy (HBE) calculations on Pt(111) show that cation identity (Li+, Na+, K+) has a negligible impact on H(ad) adsorption strength, with values differing by less than 7 meV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HBE values at all three interfaces are almost identical, differing from each other within only 7 meV ... negligible impact of the identity of cation on the H ad binding strength

nodes.characterization_summary: Slow-growth AIMD simulations determine the free energy barriers for water O-H cleavage on Pt(111), finding the order NaOH > LiOH ≈ KOH, which matches the trend of computational O-H stretching frequencies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ΔG‡ values of the Volmer reactions ... sequence of ΔG‡NaOH > ΔG‡LiOH ≈ ΔG‡KOH ... vibrational frequency of the computational O-H stretching band ... in NaOH system (~3278 cm−1) is much higher than that in LiOH and KOH systems (~3200 cm−1)

nodes.characterization_summary: AIMD simulations of proton transfer (PT) across the EDL identify PT as the key kinetic step, with barriers increasing with cation size (Li+ < Na+ < K+), providing a physical basis for the cation effect.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ΔG‡ value of PT across the interfacial EDL not only is higher than that of O-H bond cleavage of water ... but also increases with the cation size in the order of Li+ < Na+ < K+

nodes.characterization_summary: Vibrational density of states (VDOS) analysis of water layers on Pt(111) allows the assignment of experimental IR bands to specific environments: polarized first-layer water, H-bond-poor gap water, and H-bond-rich bulk-like water.
nodes.evidence_snippet: theoretical VDOS of interfacial water molecules ... first layer of water molecules immediately next to the electrode surface (denoted as AM.H2O(Pt)) ... H-bond-poor interfacial water molecules ... H-bond-rich interfacial water molecules
